serverExecution.architecture: Single Node HTTP service with a bounded FIFO task queue and dedicated calculation child processes; no client fallback.
serverExecution.persistence: Inputs, result points and status live in SIM_DATA_DIR, default .runtime/tasks. One service instance per directory.
serverExecution.recovery: Closing the page does not cancel accepted tasks. Completed results survive service restart; unfinished tasks are marked interrupted, not checkpoint-resumed.
serverExecution.access: Session-scoped task ownership and optional shared access key; no multi-user accounts/SSO. Use HTTPS and an access key before exposing beyond loopback.
serverExecution.limits: Concurrency, task time, V8 old-space, body/result size, retained task count and TTL are configurable. These are not OS-level CPU/RSS isolation.
serverExecution.strategies: Remote execution accepts DSL only. Trusted JS remains available through the explicitly opted-in local CLI.
serverExecution.batching: Each accepted batch executes points sequentially in one child process; independent tasks can execute concurrently. No single-simulation parallel speedup is claimed.

historicalTools.scripts/legacy/sim: Loading migrated to shared modules; existing numeric/reporting defects were not corrected.
historicalTools.scripts/legacy/verify: Historical HTML-scraping scripts remain unchanged and are not current entrypoints. Use npm test and npm run test:browser for maintained regression coverage.
historicalTools.scripts/legacy/debug: Historical exploratory tools were not migrated.

knownIssuesOutsideScope: Historical sim_harness.js and sim_sens_l3.js call hitRate.toFixed although hitRate is an object; preserved as pre-existing output defects.
Historical report regression E9 has three failures against an older model version; see legacy/verification-status.json.

The browser scan Worker scheduler was replaced with server batch tasks; metric mapping, point caches and chart calculations were retained. File persistence currently uses synchronous I/O and requires fast local storage.
ECharts remains at 5.5.0 for compatibility and has a moderate XSS advisory GHSA-fgmj-fm8m-jvvx. Do not use untrusted strategies or report inputs.
Capacity limits and simulation algorithm were not changed or benchmarked for larger workloads.
